SMTO-GML-0010 — SMTO couldn't tell which emails you wanted to change

GUID: d80a3d51-7653-4d2d-b3ba-c4b00fc3c081
Slug: gmail-bulk-selection-invalid
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to change a group of emails, but the request named specific emails and also a search at the same time. SMTO stopped before changing anything in your mailbox.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO again and describe the emails one way only, for example "all unread emails from the newsletter sender" or "the three emails I just listed", not both. SMTO can choose emails either by a search or by an exact list, and mixing the two makes the choice unclear.
  2. Read the preview SMTO shows, including how many emails it found, before you approve the change. The preview is the exact set that will change, so checking it makes sure only the emails you meant are affected.
  3. If you asked to mark all emails as read, or to empty Trash or Spam, ask for just that, without naming particular emails or a search. Those actions already choose their own emails, so adding a list or search makes the request unclear.
  4. If your mailbox changed since you first asked (emails moved, deleted or labeled), ask SMTO to search again instead of reusing its earlier list. An old list may no longer match the emails that are in your mailbox now.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows a preview with the number of matching emails, and after you approve, it reports the change as done.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve a change if the preview shows emails you didn't mean to include.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail bulk change was rejected before any mailbox change because its selection was invalid: message_ids were combined with query or label_ids, a fixed action (mark_all_read, empty_trash, empty_spam) was given its own selector, or an internal batch fell outside its allowed ID count.

What this means

  • Bulk operation arguments combine explicit message_ids with query or label_ids. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Bulk operation arguments combine explicit message_ids with query or label_ids.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect selection fields and choose one supported selection mode.

How to fix it

  • NativeGmailCapability.execute rejects preview_modify/batch_modify arguments that set message_ids together with query or label_ids; workflows.selection_arguments rejects query/message_ids/thread_ids on mark_all_read, empty_trash and empty_spam; rest_workflows rejects multipart batches outside 1-50 calls and ID batches outside 1-1,000. Resubmit with exactly one selection method (explicit message_ids, or query/label_ids through gmail.preview_modify then gmail.batch_modify with that preview's selection_token), and call fixed actions with no selector.
  • Generate a fresh supported selection and confirm its preview.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • One unambiguous selection method validates before preview or mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
